name: Shuri

summary: Shuri is a princess of Wakanda and the only child King T'Chaka had with Queen Ramonda. Her father was murdered by the colonialist Ulysses Klaw before she was born, so she grew up without him while his brother S'Yan reluctantly ruled as interim king and Black Panther, fighting off a stream of challengers for a title he had never wanted. From early childhood Shuri wanted that title for herself. Over her mother's objections she forced her way into the challenge arena to take on her uncle, but before she could fight, she watched her older half-brother T'Challa defeat S'Yan and win the mantle.

Living in T'Challa's shadow, Shuri was routinely kept out of matters of state by a family that wanted her safe, and she threw herself into the study of nuclear physics instead. When Wakanda's vibranium seemed to be behind a run of disasters, she suggested the metal had been tampered with, and her brother ignored her. She was right: Klaw invaded with an army of hired super-villains and quiet backing from foreign governments. At her research site the Radioactive Man killed a miner in front of her and prepared a nuclear blast, and Shuri, who had gone into hiding, came back armed with the Black Knight's Ebony Blade and killed him.

Taking a life weighed heavily on her, and she spent a period in the United States to recover. T'Challa then trained her in unarmed combat, partly so she could take his place as Black Panther if Wakanda ever needed her to. Hot-headed and quick to anger, she nonetheless grew into a formidable fighter, driven by the same wish she had as a child. The Marvel Fandom wiki credits Reginald Hudlin and John Romita Jr. with creating her; she first appears in flashback in Black Panther #2 (May 2005), and first wears the Panther's costume in Black Panther #5 (August 2009).

comics.title: A princess who wanted the mantle
comics.summary: Reginald Hudlin's relaunch tells Shuri's childhood in flashback. With T'Chaka dead, her uncle S'Yan holds the throne and the Black Panther title while challengers queue up to fight him. Young Shuri ignores her mother and pushes into the arena to try for the mantle herself, only to see her older half-brother T'Challa beat S'Yan first and become the Black Panther.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Shuri (Earth-616)

comics.title: The Ebony Blade
comics.summary: Kept out of royal business, Shuri studies nuclear physics and warns that Wakanda's vibranium may have been tampered with, a warning T'Challa dismisses until Klaw invades with a band of hired villains. When the Radioactive Man overruns her research site, murders a miner in front of her and readies a nuclear blast, she takes up the Black Knight's Ebony Blade and kills him. Shaken by her first kill, she retreats to the United States for a while, and T'Challa begins training her to fight so that she could one day stand in as Black Panther.

comics.title: Deadliest of the species
comics.summary: Doctor Doom ambushes T'Challa and leaves him near death, and Wakanda needs a new Panther. Shuri takes the heart-shaped herb to seek the blessing of the panther god Bast, who calls her arrogant and turns her away. With Morlun, the Devourer of Totems, cutting through the army towards her brother's body, she realises she has trusted science and training over Wakanda's older magic, puts on the Panther's costume regardless, spears Morlun and leads him to the witch doctor Zawavari, whose spell sends him into the realm of Death.

comics.title: Two Panthers against Doom
comics.summary: A dissident faction called the Desturi seizes Wakanda with Doctor Doom's secret help, because Doom wants the nation's vibranium, which can amplify mystical power. Shuri and T'Challa, the only people in the palace not spied on through Doom's nanites, escape with the Dora Milaje to the X-Men's island base, Utopia. In the endgame Shuri masses Wakandan forces on Latveria's border under cover of a diplomatic visit to neighbouring Symkaria, then draws Doom out of his castle by calling on him to face her ruler to ruler, setting up T'Challa's final move against him.

comics.title: War with Atlantis
comics.summary: Ruling Wakanda as queen during a bitter war with Atlantis, Shuri hears Namor's offer of peace in return for the right to take refuge in Wakanda whenever he chooses. Like T'Challa before her she refuses, convinced the conflict can only end with one of the two nations destroyed. While Namor celebrates a truce he believes he has made, he learns it was never real and finds Atlantis left in ruins by Shuri's forces.

comics.title: Last stand in the Necropolis
comics.summary: As colliding universes threaten Earth, Namor's Cabal takes over Wakanda as a base for destroying the incoming worlds, razing the Golden City. Shuri and T'Challa lead a strike on the Necropolis to sabotage the Cabal's stolen planet-killing bombs, but the raid is a trap and Proxima Midnight slaughters their soldiers. Shuri tells her brother to teleport out and stays behind to face their enemies alone.

comics.title: The Ancient Future
comics.summary: Beaten by the Cabal, Shuri is sealed in an amber-like stasis described as a living death, while her spirit travels to the Djalia, the plane that holds Wakanda's collective memory, and learns from a griot that has taken her mother's form. T'Challa recovers her soul with the help of the teleporter Manifold, and she comes back with mystical abilities, among them turning into a flock of birds or into living stone, and with a new role as the Aja-Adanna, keeper of Wakandan lore. Soon after, she persuades the rebel Dora Milaje leaders Aneka and Ayo to side with the Black Panther against Tetu's uprising.

comics.title: Gadgets and the plane of memory
comics.summary: In her first solo series, written by Nnedi Okorafor, T'Challa goes missing on a space mission and Wakanda turns to Shuri, who would much rather be building gauntlets and flying gear in her lab. The run gives her a redesign that brings her closer to the film version of the character. In a later arc something begins stealing pieces of the Djalia, and Shuri takes up the Panther role again in a new suit, learns to move herself and others in and out of the plane of memory, and fights to save it and the Great Mound's vibranium.

comics.title: Decoy on Wakanda Prime
comics.summary: With Wakanda back under a monarchy, Shuri helps T'Challa govern the Intergalactic Empire of Wakanda. When the Galactic Council's fleet attacks, she poses as the Black Panther to buy time, is captured and questioned by Star-Lord and Nova, and shows that the vibranium bullet blamed on Wakanda is a cheap imitation. After hidden Skrulls turn on the fleet, the three revive the Xandarian Worldmind, learn the Inhumans are behind the plot and fight their way onto the Fulcrum; afterwards she keeps the Inhumans' role secret at her brother's request, telling a frustrated Nova that her loyalty is to Wakanda rather than to justice.

screen.title: Black Panther
screen.summary: Shuri is introduced as T'Challa's teasing younger sister and the head of the Wakandan Design Group, who kits him out with a nanotech Panther Habit, remotely drives a car through Busan during the chase after Klaue and heals a badly wounded Everett Ross. When Killmonger takes the throne she flees to the Jabari with Ramonda, Nakia and Ross, helps revive T'Challa with the heart-shaped herb and fights at Mount Bashenga, and at the end T'Challa puts her in charge of science at Wakanda's new outreach centre in Oakland. In the end-credits scene she checks on Bucky Barnes as he recovers in Wakanda.

screen.title: Avengers: Infinity War
screen.summary: The Avengers bring Vision to Wakanda so that Shuri can try to remove the Mind Stone from his head without killing him, and she works on the extraction in her lab while the battle rages outside. Corvus Glaive breaks in and overpowers her before she can finish; Avengers: Endgame later confirms she was among those erased by Thanos' snap.

screen.title: Avengers: Endgame
screen.summary: Restored five years after the Snap, Shuri steps through a sorcerer's portal with T'Challa and Okoye to join the final battle, where she fights with her gauntlets and joins Pepper Potts and Hope van Dyne in a combined blast that knocks Thanos away from Carol Danvers. Afterwards she is seen reunited with her mother in Wakanda and standing with T'Challa and Okoye at Tony Stark's funeral.

screen.title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
screen.summary: After failing to save T'Challa from a fatal illness with a synthetic heart-shaped herb, Shuri is drawn into conflict with Namor of Talokan, who wants the American student behind a vibranium detector; she is taken to his underwater kingdom, and Namor's attack on the capital costs Ramonda her life. Shuri recreates the herb, meets Killmonger on the ancestral plane, becomes the new Black Panther and beats Namor in the desert, but spares him in return for peace and then skips her own coronation, leaving the throne open to M'Baku. In the mid-credits scene in Haiti she burns her mourning gown and meets Nakia's son Toussaint, who turns out to be T'Challa's child.

unverified: Avengers: Doomsday, Avengers: Secret Wars and Black Panther III appear in the MCU Wiki infobox for Shuri but are marked unreleased, so they are left out. No plot details were researched.

Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Endgame page lists only Mobius, Ouroboros, Casey, Ralph and Miss Minutes as Encore-exclusive cast, and the Encore plot extension (Steve and Peggy, Banner, the TVA, Doom) does not include Shuri. She is in the main film that the Encore repeats, so no separate entry was added.

Skipped MCU listings that are not physical appearances: WandaVision (memory), The Falcon and The Winter Soldier (mentioned), Loki (archive audio), Ms. Marvel (depiction), She-Hulk: Attorney at Law (photo), Ironheart (the episode "Take Me Home" uses archive footage of her, and a later episode only mentions her), Wonder Man (photo) and VisionQuest (footage). The Legends docuseries episode "Princess Shuri" is a recap, not new footage. VisionQuest's release status was not checked because footage is excluded either way.
Animation and voice-only work is excluded under the brief (including What If...? and Eyes of Wakanda) and was not researched.

Avengers: Damage Control (a virtual-reality experience) has its own Shuri on the Marvel Fandom wiki (Earth-TRN1569). It is not a film or series, so it is left out. No other live-action version of Shuri outside the MCU was found on the wiki's disambiguation page.

Cameo flag for Avengers: Endgame is a judgement call: Wright is in the main cast list, but Shuri only has brief moments in the final battle, the Wakanda reunion and the funeral. Infinity War is marked as a full role.
Two MCU Wiki details come from deleted scenes and are not used: Shuri kneeling to Tony Stark after the battle in Endgame, and a farewell with Okoye in Haiti in Wakanda Forever.
Infinity War itself does not show Shuri turning to dust; the MCU Wiki sources her death in the Snap to Avengers: Endgame, and the summary says so.

First appearance: the wiki lists Black Panther Vol 4 #2 (May 2005), where she appears only in flashback. It gives Black Panther Vol 5 #5 (August 2009) as her first appearance as Black Panther, although the solicitation for Vol 5 #1 already teases a female Panther.

The Earth-616 character page skips most of her career (her 2009 Panther run, Doomwar, the 2018 solo series and later stories). Those eras were built from the issue pages instead. Black Panther Vol 4 #2, #4, #6, #10 and #20, Black Panther Vol 6 #2, #8 and #10, and Shuri #1, #8 and #10 have no plot synopsis, so details from them rest on the character page (history, powers and notes) and the solicitations.

Small conflict in Imperial: the character page says Shuri promised to ask T'Challa to pay for the Worldmind, while the Imperial #3 synopsis says she declined to speak for the Black Panther and Star-Lord pledged Spartax's money. The era avoids the point.

Left out for lack of detail: the wiki lists her as a former symbiote host, citing King in Black: Black Panther #1 (April 2021), but that issue page has only a solicitation. Her other appearances after 2019 that the character page does not describe were not checked.
The Earth-616 infobox also lists a half-brother Jakarra and an adopted brother Hunter; the origin calls her T'Chaka and Ramonda's only child, as the history section does.
